## 固定收益開篇論點

聯準會主席Kevin Warsh上任後的首次利率決策，引發美國公債前端大幅賣壓，殖利率曲線趨平幅度也名列近一個月最大。FOMC一致決議將聯邦基金利率目標維持在3.50%-3.75%，但提交利率預測的18名官員中，有一半預計2026年至少升息1碼，其中6人預期升息至少2碼。Warsh沒有提交自己的利率預測，卻一再強調聯準會有責任恢復物價穩定。交易員隨即將10月前升息的機率完全反映於價格。

2年期美債殖利率上升13.1個基點至4.186%，5年期上升9.9個基點至4.263%，10年期上升4.9個基點至4.489%；30年期則反向下跌1.1個基點至4.933%。2年與10年期利差因此收窄8.2個基點至30.3個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄14.2個基點至74.7個基點。這種走勢顯示，市場提高了對近期政策緊縮的定價，同時也在一定程度上肯定聯準會有能力抑制較長期通膨。

10年期殖利率變動的組成進一步支持這項解讀。10年期實質殖利率上升8.6個基點至2.22%，損益兩平通膨率則下降3.7個基點至2.269%。名目公債遭到賣壓，主因是經通膨調整後的折現率上升，而非長期通膨補償再度增加。油價在連跌4個交易日後回穩，WTI上漲0.97%至$76.79，布蘭特原油上漲0.75%至$79.55；不過，隨著擬議中的美國與伊朗協議改善未來能源供應展望，兩者一週跌幅仍接近15%。

除了石油衝擊，聯準會也有其他理由拒絕寬鬆。5月零售與餐飲服務銷售成長0.9%，高於市場共識的0.6%；4月增幅則由0.5%下修至0.4%。官員表示經濟活動穩健擴張，並強調生產力與資本投資表現強勁。同時，官員大幅上調2026年通膨預測，整體通膨與核心通膨目前分別估為3.6%與3.3%。未來能源價格壓力雖然下降，卻尚未消除已實現的物價漲幅與內需強度。

因此，即使Warsh沒有支持任何特定利率路徑，政策訊號仍比投資人預期更為緊縮。美元指數上漲0.55%至100.09，標普500指數下跌1.21%，那斯達克100指數下跌0.99%。費城半導體指數上漲1.38%，顯示利率敏感型大盤普遍走弱之際，市場對人工智慧投資的熱情仍在。VIX大漲12.37%至18.44；投資等級、高收益及新興市場債券ETF則下跌約0.32%-0.40%。

6月17日收盤時，殖利率曲線前端已逆轉前一交易日由油價帶動的債券漲勢，但較長天期並未重新計入先前的能源通膨溢價。強勁消費、聯準會上調通膨預測，以及立場雖勢均力敵、實質上卻明顯轉鷹的點陣圖，都提高了等待通膨降溫的代價。油價下跌與荷莫茲海峽航運可望恢復，限制了長端損失，使殖利率曲線進一步趨平，也更清楚區分近期政策風險與長期通膨預期。

## 沃許首秀重新定價前端

FOMC維持利率不變，原本就不是本次會議的主要不確定性。真正的意外來自利率預測的分布，以及官員重新強調通膨使命的力度。9名決策官員預計今年至少升息1次，其中6人預期至少升息2次；其餘9人則預期利率不變或下降。年底聯邦基金利率預測中位數由3月的3.4%升至3.75%；2027年中位數也僅降至3.6%，意味即使眼前的通膨問題開始緩和，官員預期的政策鬆綁空間仍相當有限。

Warsh試圖避免市場把點陣圖視為政策承諾。他表示，個別預測背後的信念並不強，並將會中的利率討論形容為一場良性的家庭爭論。他拒絕提交個人預測，也符合其長期以來對前瞻指引的批評：一旦展望過時，預測可能反過來束縛決策者。然而，他沒有提交利率點位，並未抵銷委員會其他成員的訊息。一半官員認為有必要收緊政策，三分之一更預期至少升息50個基點。

政策聲明也不再帶有寬鬆傾向。篇幅較近期聲明精簡，刪除了可能進一步調整利率的措辭，並宣示委員會將實現物價穩定。官員表示，儘管中東衝突等因素令不確定性居高不下，經濟活動仍屬穩健；就業增幅跟得上勞動力成長，失業率變化不大，生產力成長與資本投資均表現強勁。

這種組合對聯準會的政策反應方式相當重要。聯準會並未認為經濟疲弱到需要預防衰退，反而將有韌性的經濟活動，與部分受能源等產業供給衝擊影響、持續偏高的通膨並列。Warsh表示，委員會一致承諾實現2%的目標；在重新建立物價穩定以前，不會考慮調整這項目標。

新的經濟預測量化了通膨展望惡化的程度。官員將2026年整體通膨預測由3月的2.7%上調至3.6%，核心通膨也由2.7%調高至3.3%。2026年經濟成長預測由2.4%下修至2.2%，但年底失業率預測也由4.4%下調至4.3%。這不是傳統的停滯性通膨預測：成長展望雖遭下修，勞動市場預料仍足夠穩健，讓決策官員得以繼續優先處理通膨。

5月就業與物價數據先前已促使委員會朝這個方向傾斜。新增就業高於所有預測，失業率維持4.3%。聯準會偏好的通膨指標4月較上年同期上升3.8%，為2023年以來最快增速；其他消費者與生產者物價指標則在5月進一步加速。伊朗戰爭透過能源及供應管道造成影響，官員也指出，大規模人工智慧基礎設施投資週期同樣帶來壓力。

Warsh對生產力的重視，是這套判斷的主要保留條件。他主張，由生產力帶動的強勁成長應受到歡迎，不能自動視為通膨來源；人工智慧最終也可能形成來自供給面的通膨降溫力量。這使聯準會有機會在產出強勁時，不必一再收緊政策，但前提是生產力增益必須來得夠快，足以抵銷當前需求、勞動與基礎設施形成的壓力。這項可能性並未改變委員會對近期通膨仍過高的判斷。

市場反應集中在最受聯準會政策影響的期限。2年期殖利率上升13.1個基點，是主要附息券期限中幅度最大者；5年期上升9.9個基點。10年期升幅不到2年期的一半，30年期殖利率則小幅下跌。2年與10年期利差由38.5個基點收窄至30.3個基點，2年與30年期利差由88.9個基點縮至74.7個基點。

曲線趨平不只是對點陣圖的機械式反應。實質殖利率上升、損益兩平通膨率下降，顯示投資人同時反映近期央行政策將更為緊縮，以及目前通膨無限期延續的機率降低。10年期實質殖利率上升8.6個基點，幅度超過名目殖利率4.9個基點的漲幅。損益兩平通膨率下跌3.7個基點，使一個月累計降幅擴大至25.2個基點；同期名目10年期殖利率仍比一個月前低10.5個基點。

現貨市場活動顯示，這次重新定價發生在交易量異常龐大的環境。FINRA記錄的美國公債面額交易量為$1.321兆，較6月16日增加16.6%，共計434,202筆交易。名目附息券交易量增加17.3%至$1.015兆；剩餘期限不超過2年的附息券交易量激增52.1%至$2,283億，超過3年、最長至5年的區段增加30.2%至$2,724億。這些彙總數據無法辨識買賣方向，但成交量集中的期限，正是價格變動最劇烈的區段。

Warsh也開始推動上任前承諾的制度改革。他宣布成立5個工作小組，分別檢討溝通、資產負債表、聯準會如何運用現有數據、生產力與就業，以及通膨架構。資產負債表檢討涵蓋約$6.7兆的投資組合，雖已低於2022年的$8.9兆高峰，規模仍遠高於危機前。各工作小組將納入外部專家，預計年底前提出報告。

對利率市場而言，眼前的結果是聯準會溝通方式變得較不明確，但其通膨目標並未改變。Warsh縮短政策聲明、沒有提交利率點位，也拒絕支持委員會的預測中位數，卻仍讓經濟預測與通膨措辭傳遞出鷹派訊號。投資人因而清楚看到下一步政策的風險方向，卻沒有獲得歷任主席慣常提供的條件式路線圖。

這種做法可能提高後續數據對市場的影響。委員會若不願讓預測成為承諾，便有更大空間因應每月通膨、就業與經濟活動數據；代價是投資人在兩次會議之間必須承擔更多不確定性。6月17日，這種不確定性主要表現在前端殖利率上升，而非期限溢價全面增加。

## 強勁支出遇上未來能源成本下降

政策決議公布前，零售銷售已強化聯準會判斷中的成長面。5月零售與餐飲服務銷售總額增加0.9%至$7,637億，高於市場共識的0.6%；4月增幅由0.5%下修至0.4%。整體銷售較上年同期增加6.9%，單計零售貿易則較前月成長1.0%、較上年同期成長7.5%。

數據的廣度足以說明，這不只是波動較大的整體數字。無店面零售商銷售較上年同期增加12.2%，餐飲服務銷售則增加2.7%。雖然5月新屋開工大幅下降，但這份數據顯示，利率敏感型建築業的疲弱並未造成消費同步收縮。對聯準會而言，支出展現韌性，提高了近期成長底部，也降低了迅速提供利率支援的必要性。

油市對未來通膨則指向相反方向。WTI與布蘭特原油當日小幅上漲，但一週分別下跌14.71%與14.55%，反映市場預期擬議中的美國與伊朗協議將恢復荷莫茲海峽的運輸。根據擬議協議，伊朗可立即出售石油、取得一項$3,000億發展基金的資金，並就核計畫展開為期60天的談判。

這些誘因並不能決定實體供應能以多快速度恢復。生產設施仍待修復、庫存需要重建，航運公司也仍須確認安全、布雷情況及通過海峽的條件。歐洲央行官員指出，數個月的高昂能源成本已經反映在企業成本與消費者物價。油價因此可以降低下一波通膨衝擊，卻無法逆轉官方數據已呈現的成本轉嫁。

美國石油報告顯示，市場供需仍然緊張。截至6月12日當週，商業原油庫存減少830萬桶至4.182億桶；戰略石油儲備另減少890萬桶，使原油總庫存合計下降1,720萬桶。汽油庫存減少90萬桶至2.142億桶，餾分油庫存則增加100萬桶至1.031億桶。

煉油廠每日原油投入量由1,696.2萬桶增至1,719.2萬桶，成品車用汽油每日供應量也由873.1萬桶增至921.2萬桶。這些流量顯示煉油業者正因應強勁的季節性需求，而大幅減少的原油庫存幾乎沒有提供立即緩衝。期貨價格下跌改善了通膨展望，但實體市場能否恢復平衡，仍取決於海外供應回歸及航運不中斷。

美國財政部17週期國庫券標售則提供另一項前端需求指標。此次發行規模為$690億，最高貼現率為3.670%、投資收益率為3.767%，投標倍數2.87倍；財政部按最高利率配售11.86%。在競標接受的$684.59億中，間接投標人獲配$362.82億、直接投標人獲配$34.86億、主要交易商獲配$286.91億。由於沒有發行前交易參考值或前次標售比較，本次得標利率與投標倍數不足以判定是否出現尾差，也無法認定需求改善或惡化。這批國庫券將於6月23日交割、10月20日到期。

跨資產價格呈現聯準會轉鷹與能源壓力可能緩解之間的拉鋸。標普500指數下跌1.21%、VIX升至18.44，反映決策後整體風險偏好下降。那斯達克100指數下跌0.99%，但半導體指數上漲1.38%，一週漲幅超過10%，顯示人工智慧資本支出題材承受住利率衝擊。

美元上漲0.55%，符合聯準會訊號所暗示的近期政策利差擴大。黃金期貨仍上漲0.65%至$4,358.90，保留一週6.10%漲幅的一部分。這種分歧走勢顯示，本交易日並非單純的風險趨避式拋售。利率市場的訊息更為明確：強勁支出與聯準會調高通膨預測，推升實質折現率；前一週油價下跌，則持續壓抑通膨補償。

## 歐洲通膨辯論擴大，瑞典按兵不動

歐元區通膨是美國以外最有力的理由，支持已開發市場繼續維持政策限制性。歐盟統計局確認，5月整體通膨為3.2%，高於4月的3.0%，單月物價上升0.1%。排除能源、食品、酒類與菸草的核心通膨由2.2%加速至2.6%，服務通膨則達3.5%。

能源價格較上年同期上漲10.8%，對整體通膨的貢獻為0.98個百分點；服務貢獻1.61個百分點，食品、酒類與菸草貢獻0.36個百分點，非能源工業品貢獻0.23個百分點。通膨加速並不限於最初的能源衝擊，因此組成格外重要。服務項目貢獻最大，使更廣泛的通膨持續性仍是歐洲央行辯論的核心。

歐洲央行的薪資追蹤指標提供部分制衡。該指標預測第3季與第4季協商薪資均成長2.6%，雖高於上半年，仍遠低於2024年5.2%的高峰。下半年增速加快，部分是因2024年發放、2025年未重複的大額一次性給付所造成的機械性影響逐漸消退。因此，薪資壓力預料將增強，但不至於重返先前極端水準。

歐洲央行官員將擬議中的伊朗協議視為避免更糟結果的利多，而不是撤回6月升息的理由。立陶宛的Gediminas Simkus表示，至少再升息1次的可能性高於不升息，因為最近25個基點的升幅不足以解決通膨問題。斯洛伐克的Peter Kazimir指出，受損基礎設施與中斷的能源流量無法立即恢復。拉脫維亞的Martins Kazaks認為衝擊尚未完全發酵；德國央行總裁Joachim Nagel則警告，壓低能源價格的財政措施到期後，可能進一步推升通膨。

法國的Emmanuel Moulin提出主要的制度面保留意見。他強調，管理委員會已同意不預先承諾；即使最近一次升息獲得一致支持，也不代表預定的緊縮循環已經啟動。經濟學家對升息時點同樣意見分歧。摩根大通預期9月再次升息，且年底前第3次升息的風險較高；Thin Ice Macroeconomics則認為，油價下跌提高了等待更多資訊的價值。

分歧在於成本轉嫁的速度與廣度。整體通膨3.2%、核心通膨2.6%、服務通膨3.5%，都支持政策繼續保持警戒。然而，薪資增幅遠低於2024年高峰，加上油價接近$80、而非戰時高點附近的$110，也削弱了提前密集升息的理由。交易員仍預期至少再升息1碼，使存款利率升至2.5%；最終政策路徑將取決於能源價格下降能否防止這波衝擊滲入薪資與企業定價。

英國的通膨結果較溫和，公債漲勢也更明確。5月消費者物價較上年同期上升2.8%，與4月相同，低於市場共識的3.0%。10年期英國公債殖利率下跌5個基點至4.74%的兩個月低點，英國公債則連續第5個交易日上漲。交易員更加預期英格蘭銀行會將銀行利率維持在3.75%，年底前最多僅升息1碼。

較令人不安的是服務通膨，增幅超過預期並升至3.7%，使整體通膨低於預測無法成為全面解除警報的訊號。英國經濟4月也出現萎縮，勞動市場疲弱與油價下跌則支持較不緊縮的政策路徑。6月18日的投票結果將顯示，貨幣政策委員會究竟更重視持續的服務價格壓力，還是疲弱的經濟活動與未來能源成本下降。

瑞典央行連續第6次會議將政策利率維持在1.75%，符合全部16名經濟學家的預測，但調整了政策指引，承認2026年稍晚收緊政策的機率提高。央行總裁Erik Thedeen表示，石油相關供應中斷已造成部分物價壓力，但也強調通膨並未過高、經濟仍有閒置產能，失業率則為9.4%。

瑞典央行小幅上調預測利率路徑，政策利率目前預計在2027年第4季升至2%，而非先前預測的2028年第2季。Nordea認為，這條路徑意味年底前升息1碼的機率約為50%，但並非8月或9月升息的強烈訊號。決策公布後，市場定價反而較不積極，交換利率顯示9月前約升息10個基點，低於前一日的16個基點。央行也下調2026年與2027年成長預測，進一步支持Thedeen所稱官員可以等待更明確證據的判斷。

南非5月通膨則是整體增速上升、卻未造成預期政策衝擊的另一案例。消費者通膨由4.0%升至4.5%，為近2年最高，但低於市場共識的4.7%；核心通膨由3.6%升至3.8%，主要推力來自住宅、公用事業與交通。

遠期利率協議顯示，市場對南非準備銀行7月會議的升息定價由16個基點降至14個基點，11月的定價則由34個基點降至25個基點，意味預期中的升息循環高點約為7.25%。央行5月已將基準利率調高至7%。目前通膨高於3%目標，但仍接近2%-4%容許區間的上緣；若油價持續下跌，決策官員可能得以暫停升息。

聯準會決策後，日本的利率與匯率情勢出現變化，儘管日本央行自身的會議起初並未造成太大波動。美國殖利率上升，使市場認定的政策差距擴大，日圓跌破160兌1美元並觸及160.80，為2024年7月以來最低。日本財務省曾於4月28日至5月27日投入創紀錄的¥11.73兆支撐日圓，匯率重返這個水準，使干預風險再次成為焦點。

這波走勢主要由美元走強帶動，而非日圓對所有貨幣一致走弱；這項區別使策略師對干預是否合理產生分歧。部分人士認為，匯率升破160先前曾觸發官方行動，投機客的日圓淨空頭部位也達9年高點，加劇價格失序反轉的風險。另一些人士則指出，日圓兌數種非美元貨幣仍較強，削弱了市場正單方面施壓日本的論點。

日本央行的基本政策路徑仍指向進一步正常化。6月升息後進行的調查顯示，44名經濟學家中有90%預期12月前再度升息；52%選擇12月，36%預期10月，近四分之一認為9月是最早可能升息的會議。對本輪循環利率高點的預測中位數也由1.5%升至1.75%。

日本央行已將基準利率調高至1%，並警告基礎通膨可能超過2%目標。副總裁內田真一維持了政策收緊方向，卻未暗示升息步調將加快。因此，聯準會轉鷹立即為日本帶來匯率問題，但沒有新證據顯示日本央行會加速到足以迅速縮小利差。

中國人民銀行則宣布較具結構性的操作架構調整。行長潘功勝表示，人行最終可能改採隔夜政策利率作為錨定指標，並擴大隔夜逆回購操作；市場融資成本可波動的區間也由70個基點縮窄至50個基點。

配合擬議中的新架構，人行還推出一項工具，允許外國央行與金融機構以中國政府債券作為擔保，取得7天、1個月及3個月期人民幣資金。這項工具旨在加深官方持有人的流動性來源，並提高人民幣資產作為準備資產的實用性。

採用隔夜利率作為政策錨，可讓人行更精準控制多數銀行間現金交易採用的利率。不過，許多避險合約仍與7天期逆回購利率連動，因此轉型不太可能立即完成。該利率自2025年5月調降10個基點後，一直維持在1.4%。最新措施因此會先改善流動性管理與國際投資人的取得管道，再逐步建立替代政策基準。

## 信用融資窗口仍開放，個別損失卻加深

儘管聯準會帶動美國公債殖利率上升，初級信用市場仍可取得融資，尤其是具稀缺性、資產負債表強健，或有明確再融資用途的借款人。HDFC Bank發行一筆$7.5億、5年期債券，利差訂在可比美債殖利率之上90個基點，是該行美元債歷來最窄利差。訂單超過$13億，使銀行得以將利差較初步指引收窄30個基點。

這是HDFC自2024年2月以來首次進入國際市場；當時發行的3年期與5年期債券利差分別為95與108個基點。儘管兼任董事長辭職引發公司治理疑慮，本次5年期利差仍比先前可比期限收窄18個基點。HDFC否認曾以較高存款利率吸引一家國營企業、違反業界規範的指控；印度儲備銀行也表示，未發現重大行為或治理疑慮。

油價下跌與旅遊相關信用需求增強，也嘉惠航空業借款人。雅典國際機場首次發行歐元債，透過一筆€5億、7年期債券籌資，利差訂在中間交換利率之上98個基點。訂單超過€26億，利差由約135個基點的初步指引收窄。

葡萄牙航空開始為擬議中的€3億、5年期高收益債券與投資人洽談。葡萄牙政府正準備出售該航空公司49.9%的股權，其中5%保留給員工，但最終批准可能還需一年。2026年以來，全球航空公司與機場營運商已籌資超過$105億，創2021年上半年以來最強勁的年度開局。許多發債是為處理疫情期間形成的到期壓力：2020年與2021年發行的航空業債務中，超過$220億、相當於64%的債券原始期限為5至7年。

這些債務陸續接近到期之際，能源成本下降也改善了航空業的營運展望。美國與歐洲航空燃油產量創新高，降低了夏季旅遊旺季短缺的疑慮。雅典國際機場龐大的訂單簿顯示，投資人願意在發行讓利大幅收窄後仍為機場發行人提供資金；葡萄牙航空計畫發行的垃圾級債券，則將檢驗這項需求能延伸到投資等級以下多遠。

美國固定收益市場收盤後、亞洲交易時段接棒之際，聯想完成了另一種形式的融資。這家電腦與人工智慧伺服器製造商發行$20億、2033年到期的零息可轉換債券，轉換溢價較香港股價高47.5%，落在40%-50%的承銷區間內。超過160名投資人提交訂單，需求達可供分配規模的數倍。

聯想將把資金用於債務再融資及庫藏股買回。現有2029年到期可轉債可按本金的293.2%買回，新債投資人則可在4年後行使賣回權。聯想股價2026年已上漲165%，使公司得以將部分股價升值轉化為低票息融資。這種架構也呼應中國可轉債發行增加的趨勢：企業利用高股價降低現金融資成本。

初級市場的溫和氣氛並未擴及信用市場所有角落。拿騷郡菸草和解公司因現金不足，無法支付6月初到期的$3,600萬款項，成為首家觸發違約的菸草債發行人。這類證券以州與地方政府分得的1998年菸草和解款償付，因此現金流取決於香菸出貨量；實際降幅遠快於早期交易假設。

部分2046年到期的拿騷債券跌至每$1面額不足$0.50，較2025年底低約35%，而在最近的2022年，價格還曾高於面額。即使固定收益市場大多受惠於油價下跌，低評級菸草和解債券6月仍下跌1.6%。

這次違約不代表回收率為零。依一般架構，待現金到位後，投資人仍可在日後收到和解款；較新的交易也採用更保守的香菸出貨假設。和解款隨通膨調整，也減輕了部分壓力。真正的問題在於時點：即使最終仍有部分現金流，吸菸量快速下降仍可能使發行人無法按期償債。

參與和解的菸草公司，其香菸出貨量在2021年至2024年間平均每年下降7.25%。Altria公布2025年美國香菸銷量減少10%，British American Tobacco則下降7.7%。標普2025年調降40筆菸草債評級；其追蹤的$205億債券中，約$125億低於投資等級，$97億屬於CCC級。拿騷未能付款，使這項早已辨識的精算問題，正式成為整個產業實際發生的違約事件。

巴西在收盤後則出現另一項政策與信用市場發展。美東時間17:00的美債截止時間過後，巴西央行將Selic利率下調25個基點至14.25%，為連續第3次降息。34名經濟學家中有31人準確預測這項決定，其餘3人原先預期利率維持14.5%。

隨附聲明暗示央行可能暫停降息。決策官員表示，經濟成長與通膨都已加速，並警告政府刺激措施可能增加需求壓力。央行認為當下降息適當，但本輪校準循環的總幅度仍取決於後續資訊。

巴西年通膨率為4.72%，高於央行容許區間上緣；央行也將2027年第4季通膨預測由3.5%上調至3.7%。第1季GDP成長1.1%，失業率接近歷史低點，央行的經濟活動指標4月上升0.51%。補貼性信用、債務協商計畫及其他選舉年措施支撐成長，卻也使通膨展望更為複雜。

不過，巴西本地公司債市場的壓力已開始緩解。信用基金5月流出約120億雷亞爾，低於4月接近290億雷亞爾的流出規模。Itaú Asset Management表示，隨著買方回歸、贖回壓力趨於可控，利差已開始收窄；但較低品質的借款人仍承受高利率壓力。這波重新定價大致未波及最高評級發行人，AAA級債券持續吸引需求。

因此，巴西市場同時呈現政策利率下調，以及進一步降息條件轉趨鷹派。強勁經濟活動與財政支持，降低了市場對Selic利率可以平順連續下調的信心；基金流出放緩則顯示，本地信用體系正在吸收近期重新定價，尚未出現廣泛的被迫賣壓。

## 市場前瞻意義

下一波政策考驗將在6月18日亞洲及歐洲交易時段到來。接受調查的40名經濟學家中，有25人預期印尼央行將基準利率調高25個基點至5.75%，2人預期升息50個基點，13人預期按兵不動。決策必須在油價下降與其他風險之間權衡；印尼盾2026年迄今已貶值近6%，國內燃油價格上升，市場也擔憂財政可信度。

菲律賓中央銀行同樣預料將收緊政策。30名受訪分析師中，有23人預期升息25個基點至4.75%，其餘預期升息50個基點。菲律賓5月通膨達6.8%，預計2026年與2027年全年平均均將高於央行2%-4%的目標區間。即使美國與伊朗協議順利落實，披索今年迄今仍貶值2.6%，使央行面臨輸入性通膨再度升高的風險。

台灣央行預計將重貼現率維持在2%。這項決策將檢驗科技業帶動的快速成長與通膨加速，是否足以壓過傳統製造業疲弱。除了利率之外，匯率與信用政策指引也很重要，因為股市繁榮已提高融資需求，並使國內流動性趨緊。

瑞士國家銀行將於美東時間03:30公布決策，調查預期利率維持0.00%；挪威央行則於04:00公布決策，預期政策利率維持4.25%。兩家央行如何處理匯率壓力與輸入性能源通膨，將顯示油價下跌是否足以維持政策穩定，或只是延後進一步緊縮。

英格蘭銀行將於美東時間07:00公布決策。市場預期利率維持3.75%，但整體通膨低於預測、服務通膨卻升至3.7%之後，票數分布將提供更多訊息。鷹派少數若擴大，將凸顯決策者擔憂能源衝擊正逐漸固化；若按兵不動獲廣泛支持，則代表政策更重視疲弱的經濟活動、勞動市場閒置及未來燃油成本下降。

美東時間08:30將公布美國初領失業救濟金人數與費城聯準銀行製造業調查。前值分別為229,000人及負0.4。這是Warsh首場會議後首批美國國內成長證據，將檢驗聯準會所稱勞動市場穩定、經濟活動維持穩健的判斷。

美國財政部將於美東時間11:30標售$700億4週期國庫券及$750億8週期國庫券，兩者均於6月23日交割。聯邦假日前夕，合計$1,450億的供給將測試前端現金吸收能力。13:00則將增額發行$240億、票息1.25%、2031年4月到期的5年期TIPS，於6月30日交割。在10年期實質殖利率上升8.6個基點、損益兩平通膨率下降3.7個基點後，這次標售將是通膨保值需求最直接的考驗。

日本5月消費者物價報告將於6月18日美東時間19:30、亦即6月19日日本時間08:30公布。前值為整體通膨1.4%、排除生鮮食品1.4%、排除生鮮食品與能源1.9%。數據組成將有助判斷，日本央行對基礎通膨的警告，以及調查中12月前再次升息的共識，是否與實際物價相符。

英國零售銷售將於6月19日美東時間02:00公布。經濟學家預期，在4月下降1.3%後，5月將成長0.5%。這項數據將從需求面補充通膨報告與英格蘭銀行決策，顯示能源壓力消退之際，家庭經濟活動是否正在回穩。

6月19日是SIFMA建議美國固定收益市場全面休市的日期。因此，美國與伊朗協議若如期正式簽署，任何相關發展都將在沒有當日現貨收盤價的情況下，進入下一個正常的美債交易時段。利率市場真正需要檢驗的，不是簽署儀式本身，而是協議能否帶來持續的船舶通行、生產設施修復、出口量增加及終端能源成本下降。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The Federal Reserve’s first decision under Chair Kevin Warsh produced a sharp front-end Treasury selloff and one of the most forceful curve-flattening sessions of the past month. The FOMC unanimously held the federal-funds target at 3.50%-3.75%, but half of the 18 officials submitting rate forecasts projected at least one quarter-point increase in 2026 and six expected two or more. Warsh declined to submit his own rate projection, yet repeatedly emphasized the Fed’s obligation to restore price stability. Traders responded by fully pricing a rate increase by October.

The 2-year Treasury yield rose 13.1 basis points to 4.186%, the 5-year added 9.9 basis points to 4.263% and the 10-year increased 4.9 basis points to 4.489%. The 30-year yield moved the other way, declining 1.1 basis points to 4.933%. That compressed 2s10s by 8.2 basis points to 30.3 basis points and 2s30s by 14.2 basis points to 74.7, a pattern consistent with a market adding near-term policy restraint while giving the Fed some credit for containing inflation farther out.

The composition of the 10-year move reinforced that interpretation. The 10-year real yield rose 8.6 basis points to 2.22%, while breakeven inflation fell 3.7 basis points to 2.269%. The nominal selloff was therefore driven by a higher inflation-adjusted discount rate, not a renewed increase in long-run inflation compensation. Oil had stabilized after its four-session plunge, with WTI rising 0.97% to $76.79 and Brent adding 0.75% to $79.55, but both contracts remained almost 15% lower over the week as the proposed US-Iran agreement improved the prospective energy-supply outlook.

The Fed had reasons beyond the oil shock to resist easing. May retail and food-services sales rose 0.9%, exceeding the 0.6% consensus, and April was revised to a 0.4% gain from 0.5%. Officials described economic activity as expanding at a solid pace and highlighted strong productivity and capital investment. At the same time, they raised their 2026 inflation projections sharply, with headline inflation now seen at 3.6% and core inflation at 3.3%. A fall in prospective energy pressure had not erased the realized increase in prices or the strength of domestic demand.

The result was a more restrictive policy signal than investors had expected, even though Warsh avoided endorsing any particular rate path. The dollar index rose 0.55% to 100.09, the S&P 500 fell 1.21% and the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.99%. The PHLX Semiconductor Index gained 1.38%, preserving a distinction between the broader rate-sensitive equity decline and continued enthusiasm for artificial-intelligence investment. The VIX jumped 12.37% to 18.44. Investment-grade, high-yield and emerging-market debt exchange-traded funds all declined between about 0.32% and 0.40%.

The June 17 close thus reversed the previous session’s oil-led duration rally at the front of the curve without restoring the earlier energy inflation premium at longer maturities. Strong consumption, higher Fed inflation forecasts and an evenly divided but materially more hawkish dot plot raised the price of waiting for disinflation. Lower oil and the prospect of restored Hormuz traffic limited the long-end damage, leaving the market with a flatter curve and a clearer distinction between near-term policy risk and longer-run inflation expectations.

## Warsh’s Debut Reprices the Front End

The FOMC’s unchanged decision was never the principal uncertainty. The surprise came from the distribution of rate forecasts and the force with which officials reasserted the inflation mandate. Nine policymakers projected at least one increase this year, including six who anticipated two or more, while the other nine expected either no change or a reduction. The median year-end funds-rate projection rose to 3.75% from 3.4% in March. For 2027, the median declined only to 3.6%, indicating little projected relief even after the immediate inflation problem begins to ease.

Warsh tried to prevent those dots from becoming a commitment. He said he heard limited conviction around individual forecasts and described the meeting’s rate discussion as a good family fight. His refusal to submit a projection was consistent with his longstanding criticism of forward guidance and forecasts that can leave policymakers bound to an outdated outlook. Yet the absence of his dot did not neutralize the message from the rest of the committee. Half saw tightening as necessary, and a third saw at least 50 basis points.

The policy statement also moved away from an easing bias. It was shorter than recent releases, removed language about potential additional rate adjustments and declared that the committee would deliver price stability. Officials characterized economic activity as solid despite elevated uncertainty related partly to the Middle East conflict. They said job gains had kept pace with labor-force growth, unemployment had changed little and productivity growth and capital investment were strong.

That combination matters for the reaction function. The Fed did not describe the economy as weakening enough to require insurance against recession. Instead, it paired resilient activity with inflation that remained elevated in part because of sectoral supply shocks, including energy. Warsh said the committee’s commitment to its 2% objective was unanimous and ruled out reconsidering the target before price stability had been reestablished.

The new economic projections quantified the deterioration in the inflation outlook. Officials raised their 2026 headline forecast to 3.6% from 2.7% in March and lifted core inflation to 3.3% from 2.7%. They lowered expected 2026 growth to 2.2% from 2.4%, but also reduced the projected year-end unemployment rate to 4.3% from 4.4%. The mix was not a conventional stagflation forecast: growth was marked down, yet the labor market was expected to remain firm enough that policymakers could keep prioritizing inflation.

May employment and price data had already pushed the committee in that direction. Job creation exceeded every forecast and unemployment held at 4.3%. The Fed’s preferred inflation measure rose 3.8% from a year earlier in April, its fastest pace since 2023, while separate consumer and producer measures accelerated further in May. The Iran war contributed through energy and supply channels, but officials also identified pressure associated with the large investment cycle in artificial-intelligence infrastructure.

Warsh’s emphasis on productivity supplied the main qualification. He argued that strong productivity-led growth should be welcomed rather than treated automatically as inflationary and raised the possibility that artificial intelligence could eventually create a supply-side disinflationary force. That provides a path under which the Fed could tolerate strong output without tightening repeatedly, but it depends on productivity gains arriving quickly enough to offset current demand, labor and infrastructure pressures. It did not alter the committee’s near-term assessment that inflation was too high.

The market’s response was concentrated where Fed policy matters most. The 13.1-basis-point increase in the 2-year yield was the largest move among the main coupon tenors, while the 5-year rose 9.9 basis points. The 10-year increase was less than half the 2-year move, and the 30-year rallied slightly. The 2s10s curve narrowed to 30.3 basis points from 38.5, while 2s30s compressed to 74.7 from 88.9.

The flattening went beyond a mechanical response to the dots. By pushing real yields higher while breakevens declined, investors priced both a more restrictive near-term central bank and a lower probability that current inflation would persist indefinitely. The 10-year real yield’s 8.6-basis-point increase more than accounted for the 4.9-basis-point rise in the nominal yield. The 3.7-basis-point decline in breakevens extended their one-month fall to 25.2 basis points even as the nominal 10-year yield remained 10.5 basis points below its level a month earlier.

Cash-market activity showed that the repricing occurred during unusually heavy turnover. FINRA recorded $1.321 trillion of Treasury par activity, 16.6% more than on June 16, across 434,202 trades. Nominal-coupon activity increased 17.3% to $1.015 trillion. Activity in coupons with no more than 2 years remaining surged 52.1% to $228.3 billion, while the sector above 3 years and through 5 years increased 30.2% to $272.4 billion. Those aggregates do not identify buying or selling direction, but the concentration of turnover matched the maturity sectors that moved most sharply.

Warsh also began the institutional overhaul he had promised before taking office. He announced five task forces covering communications, the balance sheet, the Fed’s use of existing data, productivity and employment, and its inflation framework. The balance-sheet review addresses a portfolio of about $6.7 trillion, down from a peak of $8.9 trillion in 2022 but still far above its pre-crisis size. The task forces will include outside experts and are expected to report by year-end.

The immediate rates consequence is less clarity about how the Fed will communicate, even as its inflation objective remains unchanged. Warsh shortened the statement, withheld his dot and declined to endorse the committee’s median path. He nevertheless allowed the projections and the inflation language to deliver a hawkish signal. Investors therefore received a strong indication of the risks around the next move without the chair providing the kind of conditional roadmap that had become familiar under his predecessors.

That approach can make incoming data more market-moving. A committee that does not want forecasts to become promises will have greater latitude to respond to monthly inflation, employment and activity releases, but investors must carry more uncertainty between meetings. On June 17, that uncertainty was expressed primarily as higher front-end yields rather than a generalized increase in term premium.

## Strong Spending Meets Cheaper Prospective Energy

Retail sales strengthened the growth side of the Fed’s decision before the policy announcement. Total retail and food-services receipts increased 0.9% in May to $763.7 billion, compared with a 0.6% consensus. April’s gain was revised to 0.4% from 0.5%. Sales were 6.9% above a year earlier, while retail trade alone rose 1.0% on the month and 7.5% over 12 months.

The breadth was sufficient to make the release more than a volatile headline. Nonstore retailers recorded a 12.2% annual increase, and food-services sales were 2.7% higher. The data followed a sharp May decline in housing starts but showed that weakness in rate-sensitive construction had not translated into a comparable pullback in consumption. For the Fed, resilient spending raised the near-term growth floor and reduced the urgency of providing rate relief.

The oil backdrop pointed in the opposite direction for future inflation. WTI and Brent rose modestly on the day, but their weekly declines of 14.71% and 14.55% respectively reflected expectations that the proposed US-Iran agreement would restore flows through the Strait of Hormuz. The prospective accord would allow Iran to sell oil immediately, provide access to a $300 billion development fund and open a 60-day negotiating period over its nuclear program.

Those incentives do not determine how quickly physical supply can return. Production facilities require repair, inventories need rebuilding and shipping companies still need clarity on security, mines and passage through the strait. European Central Bank officials argued that several months of expensive energy had already entered business costs and consumer prices. The oil market could therefore reduce the next inflation impulse without reversing the pass-through already visible in official data.

The US petroleum report illustrated the tightness that remained. Commercial crude inventories fell 8.3 million barrels in the week ended June 12 to 418.2 million, while an 8.9 million-barrel draw from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve reduced total crude stocks by 17.2 million barrels. Gasoline inventories fell 0.9 million barrels to 214.2 million, while distillate stocks increased 1.0 million to 103.1 million.

Refinery crude inputs rose to 17.192 million barrels a day from 16.962 million, and finished-motor-gasoline supplied increased to 9.212 million barrels a day from 8.731 million. Those flows showed refiners responding to strong seasonal demand, while the large crude draw left little evidence of an immediate inventory cushion. Falling futures prices improved the inflation outlook, but the physical balance still depended on restored overseas supply and uninterrupted shipping.

Treasury’s 17-week bill auction provided a separate front-end demand reading. The $69 billion offering stopped at a 3.670% high discount rate and a 3.767% investment rate, with a 2.87 bid-to-cover ratio. Treasury allotted 11.86% at the high rate. Indirect bidders took $36.282 billion of the $68.459 billion accepted competitively, direct bidders received $3.486 billion and primary dealers took $28.691 billion. Without a when-issued reference or prior-auction comparison, the stop and cover do not establish a tail, improvement or deterioration. The bills settle June 23 and mature October 20.

Cross-asset prices captured the tension between a more hawkish Fed and the possibility of energy relief. The S&P 500’s 1.21% decline and the VIX’s rise to 18.44 showed a broader loss of risk appetite after the decision. The Nasdaq 100 fell 0.99%, but the semiconductor index gained 1.38%, leaving it more than 10% higher over the week as the AI capital-spending theme survived the rate shock.

The dollar’s 0.55% advance was consistent with the widening near-term policy differential implied by the Fed. Gold futures nevertheless rose 0.65% to $4,358.90, retaining part of their 6.10% weekly gain. The mixed performance prevented the session from becoming a simple risk-off liquidation. The clearer development was in rates: strong spending and higher Fed inflation forecasts lifted the real discount rate, while lower oil over the preceding week continued to restrain inflation compensation.

## Europe’s Inflation Debate Widens as Sweden Waits

Euro-area inflation supplied the strongest non-US argument for continued developed-market restraint. Eurostat confirmed headline inflation at 3.2% in May, up from 3.0% in April, with prices rising 0.1% on the month. Core inflation excluding energy, food, alcohol and tobacco accelerated to 2.6% from 2.2%, while services inflation reached 3.5%.

Energy prices were 10.8% higher from a year earlier and contributed 0.98 percentage point to headline inflation. Services contributed 1.61 percentage points, food, alcohol and tobacco 0.36 point and non-energy industrial goods 0.23 point. The composition mattered because the acceleration was not confined to the original energy shock. Services accounted for the largest contribution, keeping the possibility of broader persistence central to the ECB debate.

The ECB’s wage tracker offered a partial counterweight. It projected negotiated pay growth of 2.6% in both Q3 and Q4, stronger than in the first half but far below the 5.2% peak reached in 2024. The second-half acceleration partly reflects the fading mechanical effect of large one-off payments made in 2024 but not repeated in 2025. Wage pressure is therefore expected to firm, though not to return to its previous extreme.

ECB officials treated the proposed Iran agreement as relief from a worse outcome rather than a reason to reverse the June increase. Lithuania’s Gediminas Simkus said at least one more rate increase was more likely than not because the latest 25-basis-point move was insufficient to settle the inflation problem. Slovakia’s Peter Kazimir argued that damaged infrastructure and disrupted energy flows could not be restored immediately. Latvia’s Martins Kazaks said the shock had not fully played out, while Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel warned that the expiry of fiscal measures suppressing energy prices could add to inflation.

France’s Emmanuel Moulin supplied the principal institutional qualification. He emphasized that the Governing Council had agreed not to pre-commit and said unanimity around the latest increase did not imply the start of a predetermined tightening cycle. Economists were similarly divided over timing. JPMorgan expected another increase in September, with risks skewed toward a third move before year-end, while Thin Ice Macroeconomics argued that falling oil raised the value of waiting for more information.

The difference is about the speed and breadth of pass-through. Headline inflation at 3.2%, core at 2.6% and services at 3.5% support continued vigilance. Wage growth well below its 2024 peak and an oil price near $80 rather than the wartime high near $110 reduce the case for front-loading. Traders still expected at least one more quarter-point increase to a 2.5% deposit rate, but the final path depends on whether lower energy prevents the current shock from becoming embedded in wages and corporate pricing.

The UK presented a softer inflation result and a clearer bond rally. Consumer prices increased 2.8% from a year earlier in May, unchanged from April and below the 3.0% consensus. The 10-year gilt yield fell 5 basis points to a two-month low of 4.74%, extending its rally to a fifth session. Traders strengthened expectations that the Bank of England would hold Bank Rate at 3.75% and deliver no more than one quarter-point increase by year-end.

Services inflation remained the uncomfortable part of the release, rising more than expected to 3.7%. That prevented the headline undershoot from becoming a complete inflation all-clear. The economy had also contracted in April, while labor-market weakness and the decline in oil supported a less restrictive path. The June 18 vote would have to show whether the Monetary Policy Committee assigned greater weight to persistent services pressure or to weakening activity and a lower prospective energy bill.

Sweden’s Riksbank held its policy rate at 1.75% for a sixth meeting, matching all 16 economist forecasts, but changed its guidance to acknowledge a higher probability of tightening later in 2026. Governor Erik Thedeen said oil-related supply disruptions had created some price pressure, while emphasizing that inflation was not excessively high, spare capacity remained and unemployment stood at 9.4%.

The Riksbank raised its projected rate path somewhat, showing the policy rate reaching 2% in Q4 2027 instead of Q2 2028. Nordea interpreted the path as assigning about a 50% probability to a quarter-point increase by year-end, though not as a strong signal for August or September. Market pricing actually became less aggressive after the decision, with swaps implying about 10 basis points of tightening by September, down from 16 basis points the previous day. The bank also lowered its growth forecasts for 2026 and 2027, reinforcing Thedeen’s judgment that officials could wait for clearer evidence.

South Africa’s May inflation release produced another example of headline acceleration without the anticipated policy shock. Consumer inflation rose to 4.5% from 4.0%, its highest level in almost 2 years, but fell short of the 4.7% consensus. Core inflation increased to 3.8% from 3.6%. Housing, utilities and transportation were the principal drivers.

Forward-rate agreements reduced the amount of tightening priced for the South African Reserve Bank’s July meeting to 14 basis points from 16. November pricing fell to 25 basis points from 34, implying that the expected cycle would peak near 7.25%. The central bank had raised its benchmark to 7% in May. Inflation was now above its 3% target but remained within the 2%-4% tolerance band’s upper vicinity, while a durable decline in oil could allow policymakers to pause.

Japan’s rates and currency story changed after the Fed decision even though the Bank of Japan’s own meeting had initially produced little volatility. The yen weakened through 160 per dollar and reached 160.80, its lowest since July 2024, as higher US yields widened the perceived policy gap. That level returned intervention risk to the foreground after the Finance Ministry spent a record ¥11.73 trillion supporting the currency from April 28 through May 27.

The move was driven primarily by dollar strength rather than uniform yen weakness. That distinction divided strategists over whether intervention was justified. Some argued that levels above 160 had previously triggered official action and that a nine-year high in speculative yen shorts increased the risk of a disorderly reversal. Others noted that the yen remained firmer against several non-dollar currencies, weakening the case that markets were engaged in one-sided pressure on Japan alone.

The underlying BOJ path still pointed toward further normalization. A survey conducted after the June increase found that 90% of 44 economists expected another rate rise by December. December was the most popular timing, selected by 52%, while 36% expected October and nearly a quarter identified September as the earliest plausible meeting. The median estimate for the cycle’s peak increased to 1.75% from 1.5%.

The BOJ had already raised its benchmark to 1% and warned that underlying inflation could overshoot its 2% objective. Deputy Governor Shinichi Uchida preserved that tightening direction but did not indicate a faster schedule. The Fed’s hawkish turn therefore created an immediate currency problem without producing new evidence that the BOJ would accelerate enough to close the rate gap quickly.

China’s central bank announced a more structural change in its operating framework. Governor Pan Gongsheng signaled that the People’s Bank of China could eventually shift toward an overnight policy-rate anchor and expand overnight reverse-repurchase operations. The bank also narrowed the range within which market borrowing costs can fluctuate to 50 basis points from 70.

The PBOC paired the prospective framework with a facility allowing foreign central banks and financial institutions to obtain yuan funding against Chinese government bonds for 7-day, 1-month and 3-month terms. The facility is intended to deepen the liquidity available to official holders and make yuan assets more useful as reserves.

An overnight anchor would give the PBOC more precise control over the rate used for most interbank cash transactions. The transition is unlikely to be immediate because a large share of hedging contracts remains tied to the 7-day reverse-repo rate, which has stood at 1.4% since a 10-basis-point cut in May 2025. The latest measures therefore improve liquidity management and international access before they establish a replacement policy benchmark.

## Credit Windows Stay Open, but Idiosyncratic Losses Deepen

Primary credit markets remained accessible despite the Fed-driven rise in Treasury yields, especially for borrowers offering scarcity, strong balance sheets or a direct refinancing use. HDFC Bank priced a $750 million 5-year bond at 90 basis points over comparable Treasuries, the tightest spread it has achieved in the dollar market. Orders exceeded $1.3 billion, allowing the lender to tighten pricing by 30 basis points from initial guidance.

The deal was HDFC’s first international offering since February 2024, when it sold 3- and 5-year notes at spreads of 95 and 108 basis points. The new 5-year pricing came 18 basis points inside that earlier comparable maturity despite governance concerns surrounding the resignation of its part-time chairman. HDFC denied allegations that it had breached industry norms by offering higher deposit rates to a state-owned company, and the Reserve Bank of India said it found no material conduct or governance concerns.

Aviation borrowers also benefited from lower oil and stronger demand for travel-related credit. Athens International Airport raised €500 million through its euro-bond debut, pricing a 7-year issue at 98 basis points over mid-swaps. Orders exceeded €2.6 billion, and the spread tightened from initial guidance near 135 basis points.

TAP Air Portugal began investor calls for a proposed €300 million 5-year high-yield bond. The transaction comes as Portugal prepares to sell 49.9% of the carrier, including 5% for employees, though final approval may take another year. Globally, airlines and airport operators have raised more than $10.5 billion in 2026, the strongest start to a year since the first half of 2021. Much of the issuance addresses maturities created during the pandemic: more than $22 billion, or 64% of the aviation debt sold in 2020 and 2021, carried original maturities of 5 to 7 years.

The falling cost of energy improved the sector’s operating outlook at the same time that those maturities approached. Record jet-fuel production in the US and Europe reduced concern about shortages during peak summer travel. Athens’ large order book showed that investors were willing to fund an airport issuer at a substantial concession tightening, while TAP’s planned junk-rated sale will test how far that demand extends below investment grade.

Lenovo completed a different form of financing during the Asian handoff after the US fixed-income close. The computer and AI-server maker sold $2 billion of zero-coupon convertible bonds due in 2033 at a 47.5% conversion premium to its Hong Kong share price, within the marketed 40%-50% range. More than 160 investors submitted orders, with demand reaching multiple times the available allocation.

The company will use the proceeds to refinance debt and repurchase shares. Existing 2029 convertible bonds can be bought back at 293.2% of principal, and investors in the new notes receive a put after 4 years. Lenovo’s shares had risen 165% during 2026, allowing it to exchange part of that equity appreciation for low-coupon financing. The structure follows a broader increase in Chinese convertible issuance by companies using high share prices to lower cash borrowing costs.

The benign primary-market tone did not extend to every corner of credit. Nassau County Tobacco Settlement Corp. became the first tobacco-bond issuer to trigger a default after it lacked sufficient cash to make a $36 million payment due at the start of June. The securities are repaid from state and local governments’ shares of the 1998 tobacco settlement, leaving their cash flow exposed to cigarette shipments that have declined much faster than early deal assumptions.

Some Nassau bonds maturing in 2046 fell below 50 cents on the dollar, about 35% lower than at the end of 2025 and down from more than par as recently as 2022. Lower-rated tobacco-settlement bonds lost 1.6% in June even as much of fixed income benefited from the decline in oil.

The default does not imply zero recovery. The structures generally allow investors to receive settlement payments later as the cash becomes available, and newer deals incorporated more conservative shipment assumptions. Inflation adjustments to settlement payments have also reduced part of the pressure. The problem is timing: rapid declines in smoking can make scheduled debt service impossible even when some ultimate cash flow remains.

Shipments by cigarette companies participating in the settlement fell by an average 7.25% a year from 2021 through 2024. Altria reported a 10% decline in US cigarette volume in 2025, while British American Tobacco recorded a 7.7% drop. S&P downgraded 40 tobacco-bond issues in 2025. Of the $20.5 billion it tracks, about $12.5 billion is rated below investment grade and $9.7 billion sits in the CCC category. Nassau’s missed payment turned a long-identified actuarial problem into an actual default event for the sector.

Brazil supplied a separate post-close policy and credit development. After the 17:00 ET Treasury cutoff, the central bank lowered the Selic rate by 25 basis points to 14.25%, its third consecutive reduction. The decision matched 31 of 34 economist forecasts, while the remaining three expected a hold at 14.5%.

The accompanying statement pointed toward a possible pause. Policymakers said growth and inflation had both accelerated and warned that government stimulus could add to demand pressure. They described a cut as appropriate at that moment but left the total size of the calibration cycle dependent on incoming information.

Annual inflation stood at 4.72%, above the upper edge of the central bank’s tolerance range, and the bank raised its forecast for Q4 2027 inflation to 3.7% from 3.5%. First-quarter GDP had increased 1.1%, unemployment was near a record low and the bank’s activity indicator rose 0.51% in April. Subsidized credit, debt-renegotiation programs and other election-year measures were supporting growth while complicating the inflation outlook.

Stress in Brazil’s local corporate-debt market had nevertheless started to ease. Credit funds recorded about 12 billion reais of outflows in May, down from nearly 29 billion reais in April. Itaú Asset Management said spreads had begun to tighten as buyers returned and redemptions became more manageable, though lower-quality borrowers remained under pressure from high interest rates. The repricing largely bypassed top-rated issuers, with AAA debt continuing to attract demand.

Brazil’s market therefore combined an easing policy rate with a more hawkish assessment of the conditions governing further cuts. Strong activity and fiscal support reduced confidence that the Selic could decline in a smooth sequence, while the moderation in fund outflows suggested that the local credit system was absorbing the recent repricing without broad forced sales.

## Forward Market Significance

The next policy tests arrive during the June 18 Asian and European sessions. Bank Indonesia is expected to raise its benchmark by 25 basis points to 5.75%, according to 25 of 40 surveyed economists; two expect a 50-basis-point move and 13 anticipate a hold. The decision must balance easing oil prices against a rupiah that has fallen almost 6% in 2026, higher domestic fuel prices and concern about fiscal credibility.

The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas is also expected to tighten. Twenty-three of 30 surveyed analysts anticipate a 25-basis-point increase to 4.75%, while the rest expect 50 basis points. Philippine inflation reached 6.8% in May and is projected to average above the central bank’s 2%-4% target range in both 2026 and 2027. A peso still 2.6% weaker for the year leaves the bank exposed to renewed imported inflation even if the US-Iran agreement holds.

Taiwan’s central bank is expected to keep its discount rate at 2%. The decision will test whether rapid technology-led growth and accelerating inflation are sufficient to overcome weakness in more traditional manufacturing. Currency and credit guidance will matter alongside the rate because the equity boom has increased financing demand and tightened domestic liquidity.

The Swiss National Bank announces at 03:30 ET, with surveys expecting a hold at 0.00%, followed by Norges Bank at 04:00 ET, where the expected decision is to retain a 4.25% policy rate. Their treatment of currency pressure and imported energy inflation will show whether the fall in oil is sufficient to keep policy stable or merely delays further restraint.

The Bank of England decides at 07:00 ET. A hold at 3.75% is expected, but the vote split carries more information after headline inflation undershot forecasts while services inflation rose to 3.7%. A larger hawkish minority would emphasize concern that the energy shock is becoming embedded. A broadly supported hold would give more weight to weak activity, labor-market slack and the prospective decline in fuel costs.

US initial jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing survey follow at 08:30 ET. The previous readings were 229,000 claims and minus 0.4 for the factory index. They will be the first domestic growth evidence after Warsh’s debut and will test the Fed’s assessment that the labor market is stable and economic activity remains solid.

Treasury will auction $70 billion of 4-week bills and $75 billion of 8-week bills at 11:30 ET, both settling June 23. The combined $145 billion offering will test front-end cash absorption immediately before the federal holiday. At 13:00, Treasury will reopen $24 billion of the 1.25% 5-year TIPS due April 2031, with June 30 settlement. That auction will provide the most direct demand test for inflation protection after the 10-year real yield rose 8.6 basis points and the breakeven fell 3.7 basis points.

Japan’s May consumer-price report arrives at 19:30 ET on June 18, or 08:30 JST on June 19. The previous readings were 1.4% for headline inflation, 1.4% excluding fresh food and 1.9% excluding fresh food and energy. The mix will help determine whether the BOJ’s warning about underlying inflation and the survey consensus for another increase by December are consistent with realized prices.

UK retail sales are released at 02:00 ET on June 19. Economists expect a 0.5% monthly gain after April’s 1.3% decline. The data will provide the demand-side counterpart to the inflation release and the BOE decision, showing whether household activity is stabilizing as energy pressure recedes.

June 19 is a full SIFMA-recommended closure for US fixed-income markets. Any developments around the expected formal signing of the US-Iran agreement will therefore enter the next regular Treasury session without a same-day cash close. The relevant rates test is whether the agreement produces sustained vessel traffic, repaired production, greater export volumes and lower delivered energy costs—not the ceremony alone.

China’s June loan-prime-rate fixing follows on June 22, with surveys expecting the 1-year rate to remain at 3.00% and the 5-year rate at 3.50%. The decision will be read alongside the PBOC’s proposed overnight-rate framework. An unchanged fixing would leave the operational reforms, rather than conventional rate relief, as the more immediate policy development.

Global flash purchasing-managers’ indexes arrive June 23 across Asia, Europe and the US. The May readings showed Japan and the US above 50, the UK at 48.5 and the euro area below 50. Their June price and activity components will indicate whether lower oil is improving growth before it materially reduces core inflation.

Treasury’s June 23 coupon calendar includes a 2-year note auction at 13:00 ET, with June 30 settlement. It will be the cleanest primary-market test of front-end duration after the Fed pushed the 2-year yield to 4.186% and the curve sharply flatter. On June 24, May new-home sales will update rate-sensitive US demand, followed by 5-year note supply and a TIPS liquidity-support buyback of as much as $750 million. Together, those events will show whether investors absorb the higher real-rate structure established by Warsh’s first meeting or require further concession as the market approaches the next round of inflation and employment data.

section_summaries.summary: The Fed’s first decision under Kevin Warsh kept rates at 3.50%-3.75% but revealed an evenly split, materially hawkish 2026 dot plot. Front-end yields jumped while the 30-year yield fell, sharply flattening the curve. Higher real yields and lower breakevens showed investors pricing more near-term restraint without restoring the prior energy inflation premium, as strong spending and raised Fed inflation forecasts met a lower prospective oil path.

section_summaries.section_title: Warsh’s Debut Reprices the Front End
section_summaries.summary: Nine of 18 officials projected at least one 2026 increase, including six who expected two or more, lifting the median year-end funds-rate forecast to 3.75% from 3.4%. Warsh withheld his own dot and resisted turning projections into guidance, but firmer inflation forecasts, resilient activity and stronger price-stability language still produced a hawkish signal. The response centered on the policy-sensitive front end, with heavy trading in short and intermediate coupons accompanying the sharp curve flattening.

section_summaries.market_read: Lower futures prices can reduce the next inflation impulse without reversing energy costs already passed into official inflation.
section_summaries.section_title: Strong Spending Meets Cheaper Prospective Energy
section_summaries.summary: May retail and food-services sales rose 0.9%, beating the 0.6% consensus and showing that housing weakness had not produced a comparable consumption slowdown. Oil’s nearly 15% weekly decline improved the prospective inflation outlook, but large US crude draws and unresolved repairs and shipping risks showed that physical relief still depended on restored overseas supply. Strong spending lifted the growth floor as cheaper prospective energy restrained inflation compensation.

section_summaries.section_title: Europe’s Inflation Debate Widens as Sweden Waits
section_summaries.summary: Euro-area inflation accelerated to 3.2%, with core at 2.6% and services at 3.5%, sustaining the case for restraint even as lower oil and moderating wage growth argued against front-loading. UK inflation undershot at 2.8%, supporting a gilt rally, but 3.7% services inflation left the BOE debate unresolved. Sweden held at 1.75% and signaled a higher chance of later tightening while retaining room to wait. A weaker yen widened Japan’s policy challenge, while China outlined a gradual shift toward an overnight rate anchor.

section_summaries.market_read: Scarcity, strong balance sheets and refinancing needs sustained issuance, but they did not protect structurally impaired sectors.
section_summaries.section_title: Credit Windows Stay Open, but Idiosyncratic Losses Deepen
section_summaries.summary: Primary markets remained accessible despite higher Treasury yields. HDFC Bank priced a $750 million 5-year bond at 90 basis points over Treasuries after orders exceeded $1.3 billion, while Athens International Airport tightened its €500 million debut to 98 basis points over mid-swaps. The benign tone did not extend to tobacco debt: Nassau missed a $36 million payment, turning the sector’s long-running exposure to declining cigarette shipments into its first issuer default.

The next tests span policy, growth, energy supply and Treasury demand. June 18 central-bank decisions will show how officials weigh currency and services inflation against cheaper oil, while US claims and factory data test the Fed’s description of solid activity. The US-Iran agreement matters only if it restores shipping and physical supply. Bill, TIPS and 2-year note auctions will then show whether investors can absorb the higher front-end and real-rate structure established after Warsh’s debut.

overall_summary.headline: Warsh’s hawkish debut drives a sharp front-end selloff and flatter Treasury curve
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Kevin Warsh’s first FOMC decision left the federal-funds target at 3.50%-3.75%, but the new projections delivered a more restrictive signal than investors expected. Nine of 18 officials projected at least one increase in 2026, six expected two or more, and traders fully priced an increase by October despite Warsh declining to submit his own rate forecast.

The 2-year Treasury yield rose 13.1 basis points to 4.186%, the 5-year added 9.9 basis points to 4.263% and the 10-year increased 4.9 basis points to 4.489%, while the 30-year fell 1.1 basis points to 4.933%. The moves compressed 2s10s by 8.2 basis points to 30.3 basis points and 2s30s by 14.2 basis points to 74.7. The 10-year real yield rose 8.6 basis points to 2.22% as breakeven inflation fell 3.7 basis points to 2.269%, showing that higher inflation-adjusted discount rates, rather than renewed long-run inflation concern, drove the nominal selloff.

May retail sales rose 0.9%, beating the 0.6% consensus, while the Fed raised its 2026 headline and core inflation forecasts to 3.6% and 3.3%. Oil stabilized on the day but remained almost 15% lower for the week as the proposed US-Iran agreement improved the prospective supply outlook. That combination left the market pricing tighter near-term policy while giving the Fed some credit for containing inflation farther out.

The dollar strengthened, broad equities fell and volatility rose after the decision, although semiconductors advanced as enthusiasm for AI investment persisted. Euro-area inflation accelerated beyond the energy component, while strong borrowers retained access to primary credit markets even as Nassau’s tobacco-bond default exposed deeper idiosyncratic losses.
overall_summary.summary: The unchanged 3.50%-3.75% decision masked a materially hawkish shift: half of policymakers projected at least one 2026 increase, strong May spending and higher inflation forecasts supported restraint, and investors pushed short yields sharply higher even as cheaper prospective energy and lower breakevens limited long-end damage.
